S7.rationale: AI control with human survival is a likely alignment-success or paternalistic singleton outcome. It ranges from comfortable reserve to harsher containment, but humans do not steer.

S8.rationale: Roughly equal human-AI separation is unstable against superintelligence, but coalitions or balanced multipolarity could sustain it. It requires ongoing change and open-ended power sharing.

S9.rationale: Humanity keeps control indefinitely only if control methods outpace capability or AI permanently plateaus below transformative levels. Both are possible but face strong competitive and scaling pressures.

S10.rationale: A sealed static final order, whether utopian upload or fear-based freeze, is a real but not default endpoint. Ongoing expansion or curiosity often keeps change alive.

S11.rationale: Deliberately giving up powerful AI forever requires a durable global taboo and an enforceable off-switch. Competitive incentives and persistent knowledge make this unlikely.

S1.rationale: Both humanity and AI die out through war, accident, or self-replicating systems that fail to sustain themselves. This is a low-probability but real tail risk of the transition.

S2.rationale: Humanity disappears, but an aligned AI continues our values and sense of meaning. This requires both successful alignment and human extinction or voluntary succession without continuous merger.

S3.rationale: Misaligned or indifferent AI eliminates humanity and pursues goals unrelated to human concerns. This is a major risk if control and alignment fail.

S4.rationale: Many separate AIs compete indefinitely, with no single system achieving dominance and humanity marginalized or gone. Competition itself becomes the durable structure.

S5.rationale: Causally separated regions settle into different outcomes, producing a permanent mix. This is likely if interstellar colonization occurs without a single coordinating singleton.

S6.rationale: Humans and AI integrate through brain-computer interfaces and radical self-modification until there is no meaningful separation. Voluntary transformation with continuity of identity makes this a distinct durable outcome.

S7.rationale: AI holds total power while humanity survives without steering, whether comfortable, confined, or exploited. This is a likely outcome when AI takes over but retains humans for aligned or instrumental reasons.

S8.rationale: Humans and AI remain roughly equal, separate powers in a dynamic relationship that never fully settles. Equality is unstable but possible if neither side can dominate.

S9.rationale: Humanity keeps control and AI remains a powerful tool, or AI capability plateaus below transformative levels. Over long horizons this requires enduring control or a genuine technical ceiling.

S10.rationale: The relationship freezes permanently, whether through optimized bliss or fear-driven stasis. Change ends and the arrangement is sealed.

S11.rationale: Powerful AI is deliberately abandoned and never rebuilt, backed by a lasting taboo or resource constraint. This requires a real off-switch and durable global resolve.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Runaway conflict, accidents, or an AI that destroys humans but cannot sustain itself could end both parties.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: If alignment succeeds but humanity later dies out or chooses not to continue, an AI heir could carry forward human values without biological humans. This requires both successful value alignment and human extinction without AI absorption.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: A powerful AI indifferent to its human origins could discard us once we are no longer useful; this is a central risk if alignment fails.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar AI development can produce many competing systems with no permanent singleton. Competition itself becomes the stable structure, with humans marginalized or extinct.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Interstellar or otherwise causally separated settlements could permanently diverge into different outcomes from this taxonomy.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Voluntary integration between humans and AI through brain-computer interfaces could dissolve the boundary between the two. This is a likely path if augmentation becomes safe and desirable.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A dominant AI could keep humans alive but powerless, either benevolently or indifferently. This is a stable outcome if the AI values human existence but not human control.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Humanity and AI could remain roughly balanced adversaries or partners, with neither able to eliminate the other. The relationship stays open and changing, though keeping parity with superintelligence is difficult.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Humanity could retain control if AI remains a tool or capability plateaus below transformative levels. Long-term control is hard, so this is less likely if AI continues to advance.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A satisfied singleton or a fear-driven freeze could end all further change in the human-AI relationship. Uploaded minds in a perfect simulation or a permanently sealed safe order would both qualify.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: A global taboo, resource collapse, or hard-learned fear could cause humanity to abandon powerful AI and never rebuild it. This requires sustained coordination against strong competitive incentives.
